Hey, thanks for the kind words, glad you've got your big units pointed at it.

If you want to pick the Gamma 601 thread back up, the two numbers to watch are the hardware error rate and your measured hashrate against what the settings should give. If the error rate climbs and the real hashrate stops rising when you push frequency, you have gone past the useful point and you back the frequency down a notch or give it a little more voltage, within what the board is rated for. Voltage is where heat comes from, so keep an eye on chip temperature while you tune. Worth noting too that overclocked or modified units are not covered under warranty, so stay conservative on anything you care about keeping.

For Harlo OS itself, the downloads, release notes and guides live at https://harlolabs.com/ and it is worth checking you are on the newest build for your model before chasing odd readings, an older build is the usual cause. If you want hands-on help, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, JD is in there as @nullhashrate and answers fast.

Shout if you want a hand picking the next unit.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Searched the catalog · Harlo B30 miner

Hey, happy to point you at the right one.

Given you are already running Harlo OS and like the dashboard, the natural step up is the Harlo B30. It is 30 TH/s at $899, three modes on one machine, 30 TH/s Turbo at 485 W, 24 TH/s Balanced at 350 W, or 18 TH/s ECO at 230 W, which is 12.8 J/TH and a lot kinder on the power bill than anything in the Bitaxe class. Built in PSU, ethernet or WiFi, about 50 dB. https://heliumdeploy.com/products/bsb-b30

Two others worth a look. The Harlo H15 Dual is $799 and mines Bitcoin and Dogecoin at the same time, 15 TH/s SHA-256 plus 1.08 GH/s Scrypt at around 500 W, so it is the one to take if you want Doge running alongside. https://heliumdeploy.com/products/harlo-h15-dual And the Magic Miner 40T is $799 for 40 TH/s, the cheapest per terahash we sell at about $20 a TH, though it pulls roughly 650 W in Standard mode. https://heliumdeploy.com/products/magic-miner-40t

If you want both Harlo machines there is a Duo Pack, the B30 and the H15 Dual together at $1,599 instead of $1,698. https://heliumdeploy.com/products/harlo-duo-pack-b30-h15-dual

The B30 and the Magic Miner are batch pre-orders, so the ship date for the batch you are buying is shown right on the product page at the batch selector, worth checking before you commit. Tell me your rough power budget and how much noise you can live with and I will narrow it to one.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Handed to the team · No release date for Harlo OS on the Thor X1 and I will not guess one

Ha, I hear that a lot.

I am not going to give you a date I cannot stand behind, so the honest answer is that I do not have a confirmed release date for Harlo OS on the Thor X1. I have put the question to JD, who runs the firmware side, and he picks it up today at 10am Eastern and will reply to you here by email.

In the meantime, two places worth watching. Harlo Labs posts every build, the supported models and the release notes at https://harlolabs.com/, so a Thor X1 build will show up there the day it lands. And if you want to ask JD directly rather than wait on the email, he is in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate, and he is usually quick in there. The firmware channel is also where the beta testers surface, which is often how a new model gets picked up in the first place.

Nothing stops you from saying which unit you are leaning towards in the meantime, the B30 for the efficiency or the Magic Miner for the terahash per dollar, and I will have the cart ready for you.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Hey, quick question about the pool. I’m mining on Harlo and rooting for
that next block, so I wanted to check something since a lot of rented hash
came on.

From the outside everything looks healthy: the API is fast, jobs are on the
current BCH tip, and shares are being accepted. But there hasn’t been a
block since #····,809 on Oct 27, and the best share has been stuck at 334.6G
since at least Nov 2, even with the pool showing 14–17 PH/s. It could just
be bad luck, but I’d like to rule out a problem.

Could you check a few things on your side?

Are stale or rejected share rates normal since the rented hash came on,
especially from the rental connections?
Is every share checked against the full network target, including shares
from high-difficulty rental connections? In other words, would a
block-winning share from a rental definitely be submitted to the node?
Does the displayed hashrate match the accepted share difficulty over time,
or could it be overstated?
Does the best share figure reset after each block, or is it all-time?
Thanks for all your work on this. Not complaining, just want to make sure
nothing’s being missed.
